I5.quote: We investigate the effect of heat treatment on the structure of carbide-derived carbons (CDC) prepared by chlorination from nanosized SiC particles and on their methane as well as hydrogen storage and delivery performance.

notes: Experiments in the paper are Ar (87 K) and CO2 (273 K) adsorption on an ASAP2020 and CO2/CH4 at 313 and 333 K on a Rubotherm balance: "High-pressure adsorption data of CO2 and CH4 at 313 and 333 K up to 200 bar was obtained using a gravimetric sorption system" (main, p. 2 (J. p. 16563), Section 2). All H2 values are computed: "In theory, a H2 uptake of 4.61 wt % at 77 K and 28 bar is obtained from SiC-CDC chlorinated at 800 °C and heat treated for one day" (main, p. 2 (J. p. 16563), Section 1); "TABLE 3: H2 Uptake and Delivery Obtained from the FH-NLDFT Prediction with the Nguyen et al. Parameters" (main, p. 10 (J. p. 16571), Table 3); "Figure 9. Predicted excess H2 high pressure adsorption isotherms" (main, p. 9 (J. p. 16570), Figure 9; page image checked: lines only, no markers). The experimental H2 isotherms used for model validation are quoted from other work: "experimental isotherms taken from the literature of adsorption of H2 in carbons characterized by CO2 or Ar adsorption data" (si1, p. 1, introduction to Figure S1). Code choice: theoretical_only rather than no_conditions_stated, because the paper does report H2 uptake values with T and P, but only computed ones (I1 exclusion 'uptake that is only computed'); its H2 work is purely computational. The paper does report measured CH4 uptake and FWT (Ar 87 K) surface areas (Table 1), which would bear on I2 and I4 only if I1 were met. Not a review; not retracted (record is_retracted false; no retraction statement in the PDF).
